claims.text: The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.01% on September 16 and 5.24% on October 1 after reaching 5.29% on September 30; the effective federal funds rate was 3.88% on each reported date from September 20 through October 1. The combination of technology-sector strength with weak small-cap and high-yield ETF price proxies complicates a broad risk-on or broad demand conclusion. It is consistent with selective equity demand for technology, but does not establish economy-wide credit conditions or customer-order strength. Near-term, a further rise in discount rates can reprice both stocks before their reported orders or margins change.

Growth-led higher rates would be comparatively constructive for customer investment if joint evidence shows firm customer orders and improving activity alongside higher yields; stronger compute and memory deployment could reach NVDA and MU through orders and margins more slowly than market multiple repricing. Conversely, inflation-led tightening—indicated by higher yields alongside inflation evidence, slowing orders, or funding stress—could compress multiples immediately and subsequently weaken spending, utilization, and memory pricing. Neither path is identified by the available data.

The strongest opposing path is momentum exhaustion: RSI14 was 82.97, 21-session performance still lagged XLK by 4.5778 points, and the historical regime frequencies were not better than unconditional rates. A recent rebound can therefore coexist with an intermediate sector-relative lag; trend in the price level is not the same as leadership in every benchmark window.

claims.text: A January 15, 2026 BIS final rule moved qualifying H200/equivalent and less-advanced semiconductor exports to China/Macau from presumptive denial to case-by-case review, subject to technical thresholds and certifications. NVIDIA nevertheless disclosed that, as of the end of FY2027 Q2, it was effectively foreclosed from China’s data-center compute market and could not deliver a competitively viable product approved by both governments; it also disclosed a 25% tariff on H200s shipped under the licensing program and said it had not passed that tariff to customers.

For NVDA, a further tightening, license denial/delay, or Chinese product-use restriction can impair addressable data-center demand and reinforce competitor ecosystems; a license relaxation is only optional upside, not a restoration assumption, because Chinese approval and product competitiveness remain separate constraints. Taiwan and South Korea supply continuity is a second geographic transmission channel disclosed by NVIDIA.

Downside policy scenario: a renewed broader export restriction, adverse license decision/condition, or new constraint on Taiwan/South Korea supply would preserve or deepen China-data-center exclusion and/or disrupt components, weakening the business assumption embedded in demand-led valuation cases. View-change discriminator: an authoritative rule/license action plus NVIDIA disclosure that it can—or cannot—ship a competitive China data-center system with approvals from both governments.

Micron’s June 2026 10-Q says the April 2025 Section 232 semiconductor investigation and February 2026 announced Section 301 investigations had uncertain scope/outcomes and could lead to industry-wide tariffs or trade restrictions. It identifies transmission through higher product/material/equipment costs, customer demand effects, supply-chain changes, and mitigation costs or manufacturing delays.

MU’s supplied disclosure supports a conditional trade-cost and customer-demand risk rather than a measured current loss: a final tariff or restriction could raise input/selling costs and interfere with customer products containing Micron solutions, while no supplied source quantifies Micron’s affected revenue, manufacturing geography, or pass-through.

Downside policy scenario: a final Section 232 or Section 301 measure that covers Micron-relevant semiconductors, manufacturing equipment, materials, or derivative products could raise costs, delay mitigation and weaken demand. View-change discriminator: final government scope/rates/exclusions together with Micron’s subsequent disclosure of affected sourcing, customer demand, or mitigation costs; relaxation/no covered final action would remove this particular incremental risk channel.

gaps.description: The January 2026 BIS rule is dated primary text, but no post-January complete legal-status review is supplied; it cannot establish all current amendments, license outcomes, or applicability to each issuer beyond NVIDIA’s own later disclosure.

Neither supplied policy disclosure provides revenue by end-demand country, customer domicile, manufacturing location, affected product, or a tariff/pass-through/loss coefficient. Therefore policy financial impact and a policy-based NVDA-versus-MU preference are not quantified.

assumptions: Policy scenarios are conditional and do not assume a future license approval, rule change, tariff imposition, Chinese approval, or supply disruption.
Billing/customer location, end demand, and manufacturing location are treated as distinct; no revenue or supply weight is inferred from the disclosures.
The January BIS rule is used as dated legal text only; current completeness is unverified.
result.counter_thesis: NVDA’s January rule created a case-by-case pathway for qualifying products, so a supported license plus both-government product acceptance could restore some optional China access. Conversely, MU’s cited investigations may end without measures material to Micron. Neither result is established by the supplied record.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA’s policy case if BIS issues a new/revised advanced-computing rule or a material license decision, or if NVIDIA states that a competitive China data-center system has gained (or failed to gain) both U.S. and Chinese approval; this would change the China-access assumption.

Review MU’s policy case when Section 232 or Section 301 reaches a final scope/rate/exemption decision or Micron quantifies sourcing, costs, delays, or customer-demand effects; this would convert a conditional channel into an assessable impact.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Both companies face U.S. trade-policy transmission into semiconductor demand and supply chains, but the disclosed channels differ: NVDA reports active China data-center access constraints and overseas-partner dependency, while MU reports uncertain potential tariff/trade-investigation effects. No shared financial weight or common loss percentage is established.
shared_exposures.qualification: This is a qualitative common exposure only; it does not establish equivalent legal applicability, revenue exposure, manufacturing exposure, or policy sensitivity.

agent_report.work_summary: Reviewed the supplied BIS final-rule excerpt and the latest supplied NVIDIA and Micron SEC policy/geography excerpts. Focused on legal status, issuer-described operating channels, and discriminators rather than valuation or price behavior.
main_conclusions: NVDA’s filing identifies an already-operational China data-center access constraint despite a case-by-case licensing pathway.
NVDA’s disclosed Taiwan/South Korea supply reliance adds a distinct geographic disruption channel.
MU discloses possible tariff/trade-restriction channels, but supplied evidence does not establish a final measure or quantify exposure.
Policy evidence does not support a quantified relative preference between NVDA and MU.
agent_report.short_summary: NVDA has the clearer, currently disclosed policy constraint: China data-center compute access remains effectively foreclosed in its filing. MU’s trade exposure is presently a conditional investigation/tariff risk rather than a measured impact.
limitations: No complete post-January 2026 legal-status review or verified license decisions were supplied.
No issuer revenue, customer end-demand, manufacturing, sourcing, or pass-through weights were available for the policy channels.
This role did not assess valuation, consensus, or market technicals.

result.summary: Independent commodities finding: NVDA has a supported, indirect infrastructure-capacity channel through supplier capacity and customer data-center land/power availability; neither issuer has a sourced direct oil/metals-price sensitivity. MU’s product-memory pricing cycle is distinct from commodity inputs, and current records do not size raw-material or energy pass-through.

claims.text: As of July 26, 2026, NVIDIA reported $279 billion of supply-and-capacity commitments, stated to be primarily for memory and manufacturing facilities, and separately disclosed land, power and shell guarantees for select AI-cloud partners. This establishes that component supply and data-center infrastructure are operating dependencies, rather than evidence of direct exposure to a quoted commodity price.

For NVDA, a credible supplier or utility disclosure of delayed component availability or unavailable data-center power would warrant revisiting shipment and demand-conversion assumptions: constrained delivery capacity can defer revenue recognition and/or raise fulfillment costs. The offset is that NVIDIA has secured multi-year supply commitments and agreements may be cancelable, rescheduled or adjustable before firm orders; the filing does not quantify the net margin effect.

Micron reported raw materials and supplies inventory of $986 million at May 28, 2026, versus $860 million at August 28, 2025. This is an observed balance-sheet category, not a disclosure of commodity cost, contract pricing, hedging, energy consumption, or margin sensitivity.

MU’s relevant commodities channel remains conditional: disruption or cost inflation in fabrication materials, equipment, energy or logistics could pressure manufacturing cost or constrain output, but the available filing excerpt does not quantify exposure or pass-through. Its memory pricing/mix cycle should therefore not be treated as oil or metals beta.

Micron disclosed that potential tariffs on products, materials and equipment may increase selling costs and affect demand, while NVIDIA disclosed that restrictions affecting supply from Taiwan and South Korea could negatively affect its results. These are supply/trade-risk disclosures, not evidence that a current commodity shock is occurring.

gaps.description: No inspected issuer disclosure quantifies direct electricity, fuel, metals, chemicals, wafer/material purchase costs, hedging, contractual pass-through, or gross-margin sensitivity for either company. Thus this role cannot estimate a commodity-price impact or establish a directional commodity beta.

For MU, the observed raw-material inventory balance does not identify the materials involved, purchase commitments, supplier concentration, or production volumes; it cannot establish whether a supply or input-cost change is material.

assumptions: A supplier, utility, customer, or regulator disclosure of a relevant capacity/cost disruption would be sufficient to reopen the conditional operating-risk assessment before management quantifies it.
Magnitude would require subsequent issuer or counterparty evidence on affected volumes, duration, incremental cost, contractual pricing, and mitigation actions.
USO is only an oil-price proxy and is not used as proof of either issuer’s energy cost or commodity exposure.
result.counter_thesis: The infrastructure channel may not impair near-term results: NVIDIA’s disclosed long-term supply arrangements can buffer shortages, and Micron may offset input-cost changes through product pricing, mix, efficiency, or procurement. Neither offset is quantified in the reviewed excerpts.

review_conditions.description: Reassess NVDA’s conditional capacity risk if a relevant supplier, utility, AI-cloud customer, or NVIDIA disclosure reports a component, power, land, or facility-completion constraint. It would weaken shipment/demand-conversion and margin assumptions; quantify only after affected volume, duration, cost and mitigation are disclosed.

Reassess MU’s conditional input-cost risk if Micron or a relevant supplier discloses material/energy/equipment shortages, allocation, cost inflation, or curtailed wafer output. It would weaken gross-margin or supply assumptions; size only with exposure, volume, cost and pass-through evidence.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Both issuers identify trade or supply restrictions as capable of raising costs or limiting component availability. This is a candidate shared semiconductor supply-chain exposure, not a measured common commodity beta or a quantified portfolio exposure.
shared_exposures.qualification: Coverage is based on dated issuer risk disclosures; no common supplier weights, contract terms, input-cost shares, or realized impacts were provided.

agent_report.work_summary: Reviewed the supplied SEC excerpts specifically for raw materials and power. Distinguished NVIDIA’s disclosed supply/infrastructure commitments from direct commodity pricing, and treated Micron’s raw-material inventory as a balance rather than a sensitivity measure.
main_conclusions: NVDA has an independently relevant indirect capacity channel through memory/manufacturing supply and data-center power/land availability.
MU has no quantified commodity-input sensitivity in the reviewed evidence; memory pricing is a product cycle, not commodity beta.
Neither company has sourced direct oil, metals, electricity-price, hedging, or pass-through sensitivity in this record.
agent_report.short_summary: Commodity inputs do not presently provide a directional stock signal. NVDA’s customer-infrastructure and component-capacity dependence is the more actionable conditional channel; MU needs exposure data before costs can be sized.
limitations: Only the specified filing excerpts were inspected; no commodity market series was used as causal evidence.
No issuer cost breakdown, supplier contract terms, energy-use data, or price pass-through disclosure was available in the reviewed records.

Derivative Financial Instruments
Foreign Currency Derivatives
We primarily utilize foreign currency forward contracts to mitigate the impact of foreign currency exchange rate movements on our operating expenses. These foreign currency forward contracts for operating expenses are designated as accounting hedges. Gains or losses on the contracts are recognized in Accumulated other comprehensive income or loss and reclassified to Operating expenses when the related operating expenses are recognized in earnings. During the first half of fiscal years 2027 and 2026, the impact of foreign currency forward contracts designated as accounting hedges on other comprehensive income or loss was not significant and all such instruments were determined to be highly effective.
We also entered into foreign currency forward contracts to mitigate the impact of foreign currency movements on monetary assets and liabilities. For our foreign currency contracts for assets and liabilities, the change in fair value of these non-designated contracts offsets the change in fair value of the hedged foreign currency-denominated monetary assets and liabilities, and is recognized in Other income, net. The fair values of our foreign currency contracts were not significant as of July 26, 2026, and January 25, 2026.

arguments.summary: Review finds two material drafting issues: NVDA’s reported first-half GAAP EPS includes unusually large equity-security gains that are not reconciled to the operating EPS bridge, and the draft overstates a comparative advantage for MU’s guidance without comparable NVDA forward guidance. A minor capacity-channel claim misattributes its evidence.

claims.text: NVIDIA reported $24.140bn of other income in the first six months ended July 26, 2026, including $23.707bn of gains from equity securities, alongside $118.010bn of GAAP net income and $4.85 diluted EPS. This means reported first-half GAAP EPS is not solely an operating-demand measure.

assumptions: The NVDA scenario grid is intended as a hypothetical total-GAAP-EPS sensitivity, not an operating-EPS forecast.
No unreviewed NVIDIA management outlook should be inferred from the absence of forward guidance in the supplied draft evidence.
arguments.counter_thesis: The stipulated scenario grids remain useful conditional arithmetic if their EPS cases are explicitly treated as total-GAAP-EPS assumptions and not justified by a simple continuation of first-half operating demand.

objections.description: The NVDA valuation bridge treats reported first-half $4.85 GAAP EPS as support for demand/mix-driven residual EPS, but the filing reports $24.140bn of first-half other income, including $23.707bn of equity-security gains. claims.text: NVIDIA reported $177.837bn revenue and $4.85 GAAP diluted EPS for the six months ended July 26, 2026; FY2027 is a 53-week year with a 14-week fourth quarter. However, the same six-month period included $24.140bn other income, including $23.707bn gains from equity securities, so reported GAAP EPS is not a stand-alone operating-demand measure.

NVDA's FY2027 January 26, 2026-January 31, 2027 grid is a total-GAAP-EPS sensitivity, not an operating-EPS forecast: stipulated $8.85/$9.85/$10.85 EPS and 18x/24x/30x P/E inputs produce -31.91%/+1.05%/+39.13% from the October 2 completed close. The $4/$5/$6 residuals after reported first-half $4.85 EPS are constant-share arithmetic only and are not supported by a simple operating continuation because of the disclosed non-operating gains.

Micron reported FY2026 revenue of $133.188bn and GAAP diluted EPS of $74.33. Its disclosed FQ1 FY2027 outlook is $61.5bn plus or minus $1.5bn revenue, approximately 85.95% GAAP gross margin, and $37.84 plus or minus $1.00 GAAP diluted EPS. This provides a near-term MU checkpoint, not a comparison with an unassessed NVIDIA outlook.

MU's FY2027 grid, September 4, 2026-September 2, 2027 with exact calendar still to verify, stipulates $125/$150/$175 EPS and 6x/7.2x/8.5x P/E inputs. It produces -30.23%/+0.48%/+38.39% from the October 2 completed close; the $87.16/$112.16/$137.16 residuals after the FQ1 guided EPS midpoint are constant-share arithmetic, not management full-year guidance.

Over the exact 63-session completed-close window ending October 2, NVDA's +19.6369% return, +10.7902pp excess versus XLK, 38.25% realized volatility, and -10.5835% maximum close-path drawdown compare with MU's +9.1536%, +0.3068pp, 74.56%, and -25.4770%. This supports a narrower technical preference for NVDA at 63 sessions, not a business or fair-value ranking; MU led NVDA on 21-session excess versus SPY and both historical-regime samples are descriptive rather than calibrated forecasts.

Policy risk is qualitatively different but not quantitatively rankable: NVDA disclosed effective foreclosure from China data-center compute despite a dated case-by-case rule for qualifying items, while MU disclosed possible tariff/trade-investigation effects whose scope and impact remain uncertain. Neither record supplies revenue, margin, or sourcing weights sufficient for a policy-loss comparison.

Late-September rising 10-year yields, XLK strength, and weak IWM/HYG completed-session behavior identify competing discount-rate and risk-appetite channels for both stocks, rather than a proven macro regime or issuer-specific causality.

claims.text: NVIDIA reported $177.837bn of revenue and $4.85 diluted EPS for the six months ended July 26, 2026. Its FY2027 is a 53-week year ending January 31, 2027 with a 14-week fourth quarter, so first-half performance is not a simple full-year run rate.

For NVDA FY2027 (January 26, 2026–January 31, 2027), the stipulated $8.85/$9.85/$10.85 EPS cases leave $4/$5/$6 residual EPS after the reported $4.85 first half under a constant-share approximation. At the October 2 completed close, the 18x/24x/30x cases imply -31.91%/+1.05%/+39.13%; base break-even is $9.7479 EPS at 24x or 23.7513x at $9.85 EPS. Bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss by 7.22pp. Inputs are analyst sensitivities, not guidance, consensus, observed multiples, probabilities, or fair values.

Micron reported FY2026 revenue of $133.188bn and GAAP diluted EPS of $74.33; FQ4 revenue and GAAP EPS were $54.229bn and $32.87. Management’s FQ1 FY2027 outlook is $61.5bn ± $1.5bn revenue, approximately 85.95% GAAP gross margin, and $37.84 ± $1.00 GAAP diluted EPS. This is management guidance, not a full-year forecast.

For MU FY2027 (September 4, 2026–September 2, 2027, with exact calendar still to be verified), stipulated $125/$150/$175 EPS cases imply $87.16/$112.16/$137.16 after the $37.84 guided FQ1 midpoint under a constant-share approximation. At the October 2 completed close, 6x/7.2x/8.5x cases imply -30.23%/+0.48%/+38.39%; base break-even is $149.2903 EPS at 7.2x or 7.1659x at $150 EPS. Bull gain exceeds absolute bear loss by 8.16pp. These are analyst sensitivities, not guidance, consensus, observed multiples, probabilities, or fair values.

At the exact 63-session window ending October 2, NVDA is the stronger technical candidate: its +19.6369% return, +10.7902pp excess versus XLK, 38.25% realized volatility, and -10.5835% maximum close-path drawdown compare with MU’s +9.1536%, +0.3068pp, 74.56%, and -25.4770%. This does not resolve a business or valuation preference; MU’s 21-session excess versus SPY was stronger and its five-session relative signs were negative.

Policy risk differs in status rather than being quantitatively rankable: NVDA disclosed effective foreclosure from China data-center compute and inability to pass through a stated H200 tariff, whereas MU disclosed uncertain possible tariff/trade-investigation effects without a measured current loss. Neither source supplies exposure weights or a policy-based earnings comparison.

Rising late-September long yields, technology-sector strength, and weak IWM/HYG proxy performance support competing rate and risk-appetite channels, not a single macro call. Discount-rate repricing can affect both stocks sooner than any customer spending response; the current growth-led versus tightening regime is unestablished.

NVDA’s disclosed memory/manufacturing commitments and AI-cloud land/power guarantees establish an indirect infrastructure-capacity channel; MU’s supplied record establishes raw-material inventory but no direct energy, metals, or input-cost sensitivity. Thus commodity pricing is not a directional comparator, although disruption could weaken either firm’s operating bridge.

claims.text: NVIDIA reported $24.140bn of other income in the first six months ended July 26, 2026, including $23.707bn of gains from equity securities, alongside $118.010bn of GAAP net income and $4.85 diluted EPS. This means reported first-half GAAP EPS is not solely an operating-demand measure.

objections.description: The NVDA valuation bridge treats reported first-half $4.85 GAAP EPS as support for demand/mix-driven residual EPS, but the filing reports $24.140bn of first-half other income, including $23.707bn of equity-security gains. The draft does not reconcile this non-operating component before using first-half EPS to frame sustained operating profitability. The sensitivity arithmetic can remain hypothetical, but its operating plausibility basis and business-to-valuation linkage need qualification or an operating-EPS bridge.

The draft’s conclusion that MU has “stronger” current operating guidance is an unsupported ordinal comparison. The evidence establishes detailed FQ1 FY2027 MU guidance, but the reviewed NVDA claim reports historical first-half results and no comparable NVDA forward outlook. Recast as availability of a near-term MU guidance checkpoint, not superiority of MU’s outlook, unless comparable NVIDIA guidance is sourced and assessed.

The capacity claim says NVDA disclosed memory/manufacturing commitments, but its cited NVDA evidence describes land, power and shell guarantees for select AI-cloud partners; the other cited passage is Micron inventory/PPE disclosure. Neither cited excerpt substantiates the stated NVDA memory/manufacturing-commitment characterization. Narrow the claim to the disclosed AI-cloud guarantees and separate any MU capacity facts.
